Subject: Portal onboarding: BlueCrest - presign & hashed-attachment fallback plan

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're starting the security portal onboarding for BlueCrest and want to confirm the best way to deliver evidence across multiple portals (Whistic + Vendr + OneTrust). Two quick asks: 1) Does Redwood accept presigned S3 links for bulk evidence uploads into portals or do you prefer attachments in the portal UI? 2) We need to provide cryptographic hashes (SHA256) for each uploaded file — is there a specific formatting or filename suffix you prefer for the hash metadata so Redwoods' intake can verify integrity?

We're trying to avoid a manual re-upload if presigns are blocked by the portal. If there's a recommended fallback (for example: provide a presign first, then a downloadable zip with manifest + SHA256 in the same e-mail) that would be great.

I attached our internal presign policy and a sample evidence CSV to show what we'll produce. Happy to schedule a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Alice Miller
Vendor Ops | BlueCrest Payments

Hi Alice — thanks for the note and the attachments, received. Looping in Karthik (security ops) and Mina (GRC) so we can align on acceptance and verification flows. Short answers up front: presigned S3 links are our preferred path for bulk ingestion into our portal integrations where the portal accepts external URLs. We do also support zip uploads via the portal UI as fallback.

A few details / asks from our side so we can give BlueCrest a clean runbook:

- Hashing: provide SHA256 for every file in a manifest.csv using the filename exactly as uploaded. Column order we consume is: filename, sha256, size_bytes. If you include the manifest at the root of the uploaded bundle named evidence-manifest.csv we will auto-verify.
- Presign TTL: 48 hours by default; if you need a longer window let us know and we can generate a short-lived proxy.
- Fallback: if presign fails, upload the same bundle as a zip to the portal UI. Please include the manifest inside the zip and attach a copy to this thread for audit.
- Naming: prefix files with BLUEC_restaurant? No — sorry — prefix with company shortcode: bluecrest_YYYYMMDD_assetname.ext (this helps de-dupe on our side).

Karthik / Mina — any compliance constraints (e.g., we need signed attestations or redaction before ingestion) to add?

Best,
Rachel
Sr. Customer Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context. A couple of operational security notes from our ingestion side:  

1) Manifest verification: we will perform a SHA256 verification on every file when the manifest is present. The manifest must be UTF-8 CSV, LF line endings. We only accept lowercase hex for the hashes (no 0X prefixes). Example row: bluecrest_20260627_idpscreenshot.png,3b8f9d...c4a2,34567

2) Signed attestations: for any SOC2 artifacts (ISO certs, audit reports) we require a short attestation email from the customer PO/procurement confirming they authorized the upload and that the materials can be stored for Redwood's standard 12-month staging retention. If retention needs to be longer, we need a contract addendum.

3) Attachment hashproof: BlueCrest can embed the manifest at the root of the zip and also paste a top-level manifest S3 object with the name evidence-manifest.csv. For auditability, we ask vendors to also provide a detached SHA256 manifest (manifest.sha256) in simple text form, e.g.:

    3b8f9d...c4a2  bluecrest_20260627_idpscreenshot.png

This lets our ingestion pipeline cross-check both.

4) Fallback routing: if a portal rejects a presign, we'll try: (a) attempt upload via our API proxy (if the portal supports API ingestion), (b) if that fails, mark the bundle for manual intake and create a Support ticket with a required manual upload link and retention note. Please make sure procurement can accept a manual SFTP or portal-upload if needed.

Operational ask: Alice — can you confirm whether your EPD (engineering) team can produce the detached manifest.sha256 alongside the manifest.csv? If yes, include both in the root of the bundle and in the e-mail body. Also confirm who will provide the signed attestation for SOC2 documents (name and email).

Karthik
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
